**Aligns with:** [`ANZU_PRODUCT_NORTH_STAR.md`](../../ANZU_PRODUCT_NORTH_STAR.md) §1 (end goal: figure out how to accomplish the task), §8 (verify own work: confidence from evidence, not cheerful messages), §9 (local-first infrastructure), §15 (security and evidence platform), §20 (quality test: evidence over speculation, graceful degradation).

## Implementation Slices

**Slice 1 (implemented, `backend/app/reverse_engineering/apk_sidecar.py`):** `readiness_static()` (presence + pinned apktool SHA-256) and `readiness_live()` (tools executed, versions compared), with `android.readiness_static()` / `android.readiness_dynamic()` as the split; safe intake of standalone APK, XAPK/APKS and split-APK directories from an owner-named local path (zip-slip, symlink, 8 GiB and 50,000-file caps, per-part SHA-256 and size); apktool + jadx orchestration with `-Xmx4g -XX:+UseG1GC`, 300 s / 600 s timeouts and SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL; manifest, permission and component extraction (§5); evidence `apk_unpack`, `apk_manifest`, `apk_decompile` plus `custody.json`; REST routes `POST /apk/prepare`, `POST /{id}/apk/decompile`, `GET /{id}/apk/summary|manifest|components`; catalog operations `apk_decompile` and `apk_extract_manifest` (the legacy `android_decompile` is hidden and redirected for APK investigations); a host AXML decoder as the apktool manifest fallback; cancellation stops the running tool. Tests: synthetic ZIPs, a real aapt2-linked `tests/fixtures/apk/minimal_valid.apk`, and an opt-in real apktool/jadx run.

**Slice 2 (implemented, all of section 6):** native `.so` inventory via `apk_inventory_native(ident, abi=None)`. It holds the exclusive investigation claim (refused while a decompile or another inventory is analyzing), reloads the row under the claim lock before recording, and verifies the per-claim token, so evidence IDs and custody entries cannot collide with decompile. Candidates come from APK/split ZIP metadata only; the ABI filter is applied before any bytes are read; libraries over `MAX_NATIVE_BYTES` (256 MiB), libraries recorded at intake but missing, CRC conflicts between parts, unreadable parts and more than `MAX_NATIVE_LIBS` are recorded as unknowns, never skipped silently. Reads stream a capped SHA-256 with cancel checks and keep a copy under `apk/native/<part>/`. The in-process ELF parser (32/64-bit, little/big endian, bounds-checked tables) records class/machine/endian, DT_SONAME, DT_NEEDED, RELRO (none/partial/full via PT_GNU_RELRO + BIND_NOW/DF_BIND_NOW/DF_1_NOW), stack canary (`__stack_chk_fail` in .dynsym), executable GNU_STACK and JNI exports; when dynsym or .dynamic cannot be read it falls back to `readelf -W --dynamic --dyn-syms --program-headers` in ANZU-REA, and a failed fallback is an unknown. Shannon entropy (> 7.2) is computed over executable PT_LOAD ranges (whole file if none) on 4 KiB blocks plus the short tail block, bounded by `MAX_ENTROPY_BYTES` (64 MiB). Hints: packer `.so` names (the section 6.3 list plus DexGuard `libdexguard*`/`libdgrt*` and DashO `libdasho*` name stems), high entropy, executable stack, weak RELRO, missing canary. Status is set from the merged investigation unknowns (`partial` or `investigating`). A `reported` (or closed/cancelled) investigation is refused, so a published report's status is never rewritten. `native.json` is written under the claim lock only after the evidence is recorded and is removed again if the row cannot be saved. `readelf` comes from `binutils`, installed explicitly by provisioning and checked by static readiness. Evidence `apk_native_libs` with custody; metadata `apk/metadata/native.json`; catalog op `apk_inventory_native`; REST `GET /{id}/apk/native`. Tests: real NDK r27 arm64/armv7 fixtures (`tests/fixtures/apk/`), readelf fallback on stripped section headers, malformed ELF (big-endian 32-bit, truncated section/program tables, truncated dynsym), caps/ABI filtering/missing libraries, tail entropy, claim refusal and row reload, cancel, and stale-token release.

**Slice 3 (implemented, `backend/app/reverse_engineering/apk_strings.py` + `apk_sidecar.py`):** string and endpoint extraction (§7) via `apk_extract_endpoints(ident, category=None, limit=None)` and key-material hints (§8) via `apk_crypto_hints(ident)`. Sources: DEX `string_ids` tables of every `classes*.dex` in every part (MUTF-8 decoded; malformed DEX falls back to printable runs with a declared unknown), apktool `res/values*/*.xml`, `res/xml*/*.xml`, `res/raw*` and text `assets/`, the decoded manifest (meta-data, intent-filter deep links from `components.json`), string literals and call sites in jadx `sources/**/*.java` (line-level references), and for parts apktool did not decode the `resources.arsc` global string pool and host-decoded binary XML (the AXML decoder now keeps element text). Bounds: 16 MiB per text file, 256 MiB per DEX, 2 GiB per scan, each gap recorded as an unknown. Endpoints: `url` (XML-namespace hosts filtered), `websocket`, `custom_scheme` (`android-resource://`, `file://`, `content://android.` filtered), `cloud_service` (AWS, Firebase, Supabase, Azure, Google Cloud buckets), `ipv4`/`ipv6` (loopback, unspecified, broadcast, link-local and 240/4 netmasks filtered; private/public scope), each with occurrences, ≤10 sample references and source kinds; filtered-noise counts are reported. Crypto: Google `AIza…`, AWS `AKIA`/`ASIA`, generic secret assignments (code, JSON, `<string>` resources, manifest meta-data; a specific-rule match suppresses the generic duplicate), PEM private-key markers (location only, key material never copied), Firebase DB URLs; `Cipher.getInstance` ECB (including the implicit ECB default), DES/RC4/3DES/Blowfish, RSA/NoPadding; `SecretKeySpec`/`IvParameterSpec` from literals; MD5/SHA-1 `MessageDigest` graded by password/signature context; DEX-pool transformation constants at `medium` confidence; `network_security_config.xml` (manifest reference, apktool or AXML) for user trust anchors, debug-overrides (high when debuggable), `overridePins`, cleartext, pin-sets and expired pins, plus platform defaults for targetSdk < 24 / < 28; AndroidKeyStore / StrongBox / software-keystore / KDF posture. Metadata `apk/metadata/endpoints.json`, `strings.json` (≤50,000 unique strings) and `crypto_hints.json`; evidence `apk_endpoints` and `apk_crypto_hints` (E00005/E00006 in pipeline order) with custody events; catalog ops `apk_extract_endpoints` (`category`, `limit` narrow the returned view only) and `apk_crypto_hints`; REST `GET /{id}/apk/endpoints|crypto`; `GET /{id}/apk/summary` adds `endpoints`, `urls`, `crypto_alerts`. Endpoints and crypto hints take the same per-claim-token investigation claim as decompile and native inventory (refused while any of them is analyzing), reload the row under the claim lock before recording, set status from the merged unknowns, and mark the investigation `interrupted`/`cancelled` with a custody event on failure, so evidence IDs and custody entries cannot collide. Tests: synthetic DEX, `resources.arsc` and binary-AXML builders, decompiled-source fixtures, REST and catalog.

**Slice 4 (implemented):** device (ADB) and FFS origins for prepare_apk / POST /apk/prepare. source_type is file | device | ffs. Device: adb shell pm path <package> then adb pull of base+splits into <investigation>/apk/staged/ with per-part SHA-256, custody source_kind=device_pull and source_uri=device://<serial>/<package>; missing ADB, empty pm-path, or pull failure fail closed without inventing device data (unknowns recorded only for skipped non-APK pm-path lines). FFS: reference an existing investigation with kind == "ffs", read index/files.ndjson, stream-copy the named APK under the dump root into target/ + apk/staged/, verify SHA-256 (and size when declared) against the NDJSON entry, custody source_kind=ffs_reference. Zip-slip / size / file-count caps and the existing file-path prepare path remain unchanged. Tests: mocked ADB (pm path + pull) and synthetic FFS index+dump.

**Later slices:** smali fallback; report synthesis citing E00001-E00006; remaining fixtures.
